previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ , a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and a history of cervical spine surgery, was admitted due to worsening leg weakness that impaired his ability to transfer from his wheelchair. He had no fever or systemic signs of infection, but urinalysis and initial culture indicated a urinary tract infection with E. coli and Enterococcus, likely triggered by his chronic catheterization. He was treated with IV ampicillin-sulbactam for five days, with repeat cultures showing no growth, indicating resolution of infection. His weakness was attributed to an MS pseudo-flare secondary to the UTI. He was evaluated by physical therapy and deemed to require inpatient rehabilitation. Medications were adjusted at discharge to optimize spasticity management, including dose changes to baclofen and tizanidine. He was also noted to have a stage I pressure ulcer on his hip, managed with preventive measures. He was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with follow-up planned with his MS and urology specialists.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ year old man with MS, on self-catheterization 
regimen at home with hx of recurrent UTIs, who presented to the 
ED on ___ with lethargy, high fevers, tachycardia, elevated 
lactate, and gram negative rods growing out of urine and blood 
cultures (later speciated as ESBL E. Coli).  He was resuscitated 
in ICU while receiving zosyn, with marked improvement.

# Urosepsis: Patient presented with fever >104, WBC <2,000, RR 
26, HR 120, (+)UA, MS changes and lactate of 7 meeting criteria 
for severe sepsis.  After fluid resucitation and initial 
antibiotic the patient's condition greatly improved as his MS 
returned to baseline, his HR and RR decreased to WNL, his 
lactate returned to normal levels and his temperature decreased 
to WNL.  His urine speciated ESBL E. Coli sensitive to Zosyn.  
He received additional hydration in the ICU, but did not require 
pressors.  He was stable on arrival to the floor and was 
maintained on IV zosyn.  Surveillance cultures drawn ___, 
___ were negative.  A PICC line was placed on ___, and he 
was discharged to a rehab facility where he can complete the 
course of IV zosyn.  We recommended he stop his prophylactic 
regimen of Methenamine Hippurate until completion of his zosyn 
course, at which point he can resume it.  Regarding prophylaxis, 
this patient needs more extensive services at home to prevent 
recurrent UTIs.

# Acute renal failure: Patient presented with Cr 1.3 from a 
baseline of 0.8. This likely represents pre-renal azotemia in 
the setting of sepsis and hypovolemia.  On ___ his Cr. was 
0.7.

# Left hip wound: Patient states it is due to a fall 1 month 
ago. It is unhealed despite ___ care. It was deemed an unlikely 
source of infection given history of UTIs and (+) UA.  Plain 
radiographs did not show any evidence of osteomyelitis.  On the 
floor, wound team continued to consult.  They recommended Q72H 
cleaning with sterile normal saline followed by duoderm and 
mepalex dressings.

# Multiple sclerosis.  The patient endorsed stiffness and 
spasticity consistent with his recent baseline.  He was 
continued on his home medications.  His baclofen pump does not 
need maintenance until late ___.  ___ saw him while on the 
floor and recommended further therapy at the ___ 
___.

# Hyperlipidemia:  This issue was stable.  He was continued on 
his home medications.

# Depression:  This issue was stable.  He was continued on his 
home medications.

Discharge Instructions:
You were brought to the hospital on ___ after waking up with 
fevers, chills, and lethargy.  On arrival to the emergency room 
you were found to have evidence of active infection including 
high fevers, a rapid pulse, and fast respiratory rate.  Labs 
showed infection in your bladder and in your blood, along with 
evidence of some kidney injury.  You were given a significant 
amount of fluid through your IV along with antibiotics.  Within 
24 hours, your symptoms were largely resolved and your kidney 
function had normalized.  As your blood infection requires 
additional intravenous antibiotics, we placed a PICC 
(peripherally inserted central catheter).  As you will need 
assistance to administer these medications, we have arranged 
transfer to a rehab facility.  Staff at the rehab facility will 
continue to care for your left hip wound as well.

your admission.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Requested for PICC line placement for long-term antibiotics.

The procedure was explained to the patient. A timeout was performed.

RADIOLOGIST:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___.  The attending
was present and supervising during the entire procedure.

TECHNIQUE: Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right basilic
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after
establishing intravenous access. A peel-away sheath was then placed over a
guidewire and a single lumen ___ Vaxcel catheter measuring 47.5 cm in
length was then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in
the SVC under fluoroscopic guidance. Position of the catheter was confirmed by
a fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed. The catheter was secured
to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION: Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided ___
single lumen PICC line placement via the right basilic venous approach. Final
internal length is 47.5 cm, with the tip positioned in SVC. The line is ready
to use.
